papers.title: SSMGCN: Multi-View Graph Clustering with Shared-Specific Information Modelling for Spatially Resolved Transcriptomics.
papers.summary: SSMGCN is a computational method that clusters spatial transcriptomics data by combining multiple data views (e.g., gene expression and spatial location) using graph convolutional networks. It models both shared information common to all views and specific information unique to each view, aiming to improve the accuracy of identifying distinct tissue regions or cell types. The approach falls into the broader category of AI-driven spatial omics analysis tools.
papers.why: This paper offers a deep learning framework for spatially resolved transcriptomics clustering that could be adapted to analyze spatial gene expression patterns in brain tissue, potentially aiding in the identification of interneuron subtypes or perineuronal net-associated niches.

papers.title: DiffGSP: reversing mRNA diffusion to unlock high-fidelity spatial transcriptomics
papers.summary: DiffGSP is a computational method that models mRNA diffusion as a noise process in spatial transcriptomics data and then computationally reverses it to sharpen gene expression signals. This 'denoising' approach aims to correct for the blurring effect that molecular diffusion causes during tissue sample processing, which normally reduces the spatial resolution of transcript detection. The result is claimed to be higher-fidelity spatial transcriptomics data that more accurately reflects true cellular and subcellular localization of mRNA.
papers.why: Improving the spatial precision of transcript localization directly benefits efforts to map autophagy and mitophagy-related gene expression at fine spatial resolution around interneurons and perineuronal nets in brain tissue.

papers.title: Ten quick tips for spatial transcriptomics analysis.
papers.summary: This paper offers ten practical guidelines for researchers conducting spatial transcriptomics analysis. It likely covers key steps such as data preprocessing, quality control, normalization, spatial statistics, and visualization strategies. The goal is to help scientists avoid common pitfalls and produce more reliable, reproducible results in spatial transcriptomics studies.
papers.why: Since this PhD project heavily relies on spatial transcriptomics analysis to study neurons, interneurons, and perineuronal nets in relation to mitophagy and autophagy, practical guidance on best practices would directly improve the rigor and reproducibility of the project's core methodology.

papers.title: Huangqi Guizhi Wuwu decoction suppresses experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis by promoting PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy and inhibiting microglial pyroptosis.
papers.summary: This study investigates a traditional Chinese herbal formula, Huangqi Guizhi Wuwu decoction, in a mouse model of multiple sclerosis called experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE). The researchers found that the treatment reduces disease severity by boosting PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy, a process that clears damaged mitochondria, and by blocking pyroptosis (a form of inflammatory cell death) in microglia, the brain's immune cells. This dual mechanism appears to protect neurons and reduce neuroinflammation in the disease model.
papers.why: Although focused on microglia rather than neurons, this paper offers relevant mechanistic insight into PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy pathways and neuroinflammation that could inform interpretation of mitophagy dysregulation in neuronal and interneuron contexts within the PhD project.
papers.figure: A figure showing colocalization of mitophagy markers (e.g., PINK1, Parkin, LC3) with mitochondrial and microglial pyroptosis markers (e.g., NLRP3, GSDMD) in spinal cord or brain tissue sections from treated versus untreated EAE mice.

papers.title: Multilayered interplay between the cGAS-STING pathway and autophagy
papers.summary: This paper reviews how the cGAS-STING pathway, a key sensor of cytosolic DNA that triggers innate immune signaling, interacts with autophagy at multiple molecular levels. It likely covers how autophagy can degrade STING and cGAS components to limit inflammation, while STING activation can also induce autophagy through non-canonical mechanisms. The review probably synthesizes evidence on how this crosstalk affects immune responses, cellular stress management, and disease states.
papers.why: Since damaged mitochondria release DNA that can activate cGAS-STING, understanding its crosstalk with autophagy is directly relevant to mitophagy regulation and neuroinflammatory signaling in neurons within this PhD project.

papers.title: Multilayered interplay between the cGAS-STING pathway and autophagy.
papers.summary: This paper reviews how the cGAS-STING innate immune signaling pathway interacts with autophagy at multiple molecular levels. It covers how STING activation can trigger autophagy-related processes, and conversely how autophagy machinery can regulate and dampen cGAS-STING signaling. The review likely synthesizes evidence on shared molecular players and feedback loops connecting DNA sensing, inflammation, and cellular self-degradation pathways.

papers.title: Lipid regulation of mitochondrial function in metabolic Diseases: Lipotoxic mediators and therapeutic targeting.
papers.summary: This paper reviews how lipid molecules and their metabolic disturbances affect mitochondrial function in metabolic diseases. It focuses on lipotoxic mediators—harmful lipid species that accumulate and damage mitochondria—and how they contribute to conditions like diabetes and obesity. The paper also discusses potential therapeutic strategies to target these lipid-mitochondria interactions.
papers.why: Mitochondrial dysfunction driven by lipotoxic mediators is mechanistically relevant to mitophagy regulation in neurons, offering insight into pathways that may parallel or intersect with mitochondrial quality control in brain tissue.

papers.title: Regulatory mechanisms and interactions of mitophagy and ketone body metabolism in cardiac metabolism
papers.summary: This paper reviews how mitophagy, the process of clearing damaged mitochondria, interacts with ketone body metabolism in heart tissue. It discusses the molecular pathways that regulate mitochondrial quality control alongside energy substrate switching in cardiac cells. The focus is on how these two systems coordinate to maintain cardiac metabolic health, particularly under stress conditions.
papers.why: Although this paper centers on cardiac tissue, the underlying mitophagy regulatory mechanisms may offer conceptual parallels or transferable insights for studying neuronal mitophagy in the brain.
